sources.text:
Skellig Michael (Irish: Sceilig Mhichíl [ˌʃcɛlʲəɟ ˈvʲɪçiːlʲ]), also called Great Skellig (Irish: Sceilig Mhór [ˈʃcɛlʲəɟ woːɾˠ]), is a twin-pinnacled crag 11.6 kilometres (7.2 mi) west of the Iveragh Peninsula in County Kerry, Ireland. The island is named after the archangel Michael; while "Skellig" is derived from the Irish language word sceilig, meaning a splinter of stone. Its twin island, Little Skellig (Sceilig Bheag), is smaller and inaccessible. The two islands were formed c. 374–360 million years ago during a period of mountain formation, along with the local MacGillycuddy's Reeks mountain range. Rising water levels later separated them from the mainland.
Skellig Michael consists of approximately 22 hectares (54 acres) of rock, with its highest point, known as the Spit, 218 m (714 ft) above sea level. Defined by twin peaks and a central valley called Christ’s Saddle, the island has a steep and inhospitable landscape. It is best known for its Gaelic monastery, founded between the 6th and 8th centuries, and its variety of inhabiting species, which include gannets, puffins, a colony of razorbills and a population of approximately fifty grey seals.

stops.name: Skellig Michael
stops.detail: Skellig Michael, auch Great Skellig genannt, ist eine zweizackige Felsen 11,6 Kilometer westlich der Iveragh-Halbinsel in der Grafschaft Kerry, Irland. Die Insel ist nach dem Erzengel Michael benannt, während "Skellig" vom irischen Sprachwort sceilig abgeleitet ist, was einen Steinsplitter bedeutet. Seine Zwillingsinsel, Little Skellig, ist kleiner und unzugänglich. Die beiden Inseln wurden vor 374-360 Millionen Jahren während einer Zeit der Bergbildung zusammen mit der lokalen MacGillycuddy Reeks Gebirgskette gebildet. Steigende Wasserstände trennten sie später vom Festland.
